captions.threads:
you're one person running a music project and your releases are slipping through cracks you didn't even know existed. that's not a character flaw. that's a systems problem.

1/4 the moment you hit upload at 1am, that track enters a void. no pre-save link. no teaser. no momentum. you meant to handle it tomorrow but tomorrow became next week. this isn't laziness, this is what happens when your brain is doing creative work AND administrative work simultaneously. your creative self and your project manager self are sabotaging each other.

2/4 a release calendar isn't fancy. it's survival. mine lives in a simple spreadsheet that connects to my distributor timeline, social posting dates, and when i'm actually telling people the thing exists. i stopped trying to remember. i stopped pretending i'd handle it organically. the calendar became the central nervous system for everything that needs to happen.

3/4 what changed everything: i made the calendar visible in my workspace. every morning i see what's landing today, what's coming next week, what i forgot to post about last month. it's not about being perfect. it's about not disappearing into the black hole of solo creation.

4/4 the real shift isn't the tool itself. it's accepting that organization isn't the enemy of creativity. it's the container that lets your creativity actually reach people. solo artists who treat release management like an afterthought wonder why their work vanishes. the ones who systematize it have an actual shot.
